evidence: src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts, LoanController.lend: `if (body.days < 1 || body.days > 60) { throw new LendingError('INVALID', 'A loan lasts between 1 and 60 days'); }` is a lending policy (business rule) placed in a presentation controller.

src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts, LoanController.lend: `await this.history.note(loan.id, 'lent');` runs after `this.lending.lend(...)`. This coordinates two business services in the presentation layer, which is the business layer's job.

src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts, LoanController.giveBack: `await this.history.note(body.loanId, 'returned');` is the same workflow coordination, done in the controller instead of the business service.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: LoanController is in the presentation layer. Mapping requests to HTTP results is presentation work, but the controller also enforces a lending policy: a loan must last between 1 and 60 days. It does this in `lend` and throws the business-layer `LendingError('INVALID', ...)`. The message "A loan lasts between 1 and 60 days" states a domain rule, not a check on input format, so it belongs in the business layer (for example in `LendingService` or the Loan entity). The controller also runs the use-case workflow itself. After each lend or return it calls `history.note(...)`, which ties two business services together in the presentation layer, and that coordination belongs in the business layer. Because of these business responsibilities, the file fails the rule.

violations.message: LoanController.lend enforces the business rule that a loan lasts between 1 and 60 days (`body.days < 1 || body.days > 60`) and throws the business-layer LendingError. This lending policy belongs in the business layer (domain), for example in LendingService or the Loan entity, not in a presentation controller.

LoanController.lend and LoanController.giveBack run the use-case workflow themselves by calling history.note(...) after lending.lend/giveBack. This coordination across business services belongs in the business layer (domain/application service), not in presentation.
